newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares surge despite budget delay.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares surge despite budget delay.

text.p: Nigerian share prices continued to rise in Monday's trade as investors awaited the 1997 budget that military ruler Sani Abacha is expected to broadcast this week.
The all-share index shot to an all-time high of 7043.60 from 7018.27 on Friday as investors scrambled for hotly-demanded stocks.
The banking and agricultural sectors joined petroleum and food shares in advancing in active trading.
Okomu Oilpalm rose more than four percent on its recent impressive half-year result, adding 40 kobo to 8.80 naira.
Union Bank was 30 kobo higher at 6.70 naira on renewed interest according to traders, who said Afribank on the other hand gained 10 kobo to 3.50 naira because its stock was considered cheaply priced.
Coca-Cola bottler Nigerian Bottling Company continued to rise on its recent successful merger. It added 30 kobo to end at 30.65 naira.

Increased demand too Unipetrol to new heights at 61.20 naira, up 20 kobo. For similar reason, Total rose 10 kobo to 60.00 naira and African Petroleum and National Oil were 40 kobo higher at 46.30 naira and 48.60 naira, respectively.
Insurance firm AIICO gained the maximum five percent with a 60 kobo rise to 12.61 naira.
Guinness was four kobo higher at 8.20 naira but brewery sector leaders Nigerian Breweries was unchanged at 18.00 naira.
Losses were few including conglomerate Lever Brothers which remained under pressure, closing seven kobo lower at 19.63 naira.
Other losers were Dunlop and Chemical and Allied Products which dropped 10 kobo each to 7.50 naira and 5.05 naira, respectively.
